Rashi on Nazir 39a:1:1.hebrew: א"ר פפא אנא סברי - סברא הוא בידיה, דכי אכיל חרצן חייב שתים — על חרצן ועל מכל אשר יעשה — וסברי: אותיב ליה תיובתא משום דלא נהירא ליה מילתא, וליהדר ביה:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:1:1.english: Rav Pappa said: I reasoned - [I thought that] it was [merely his own] reasoning in his hand, that when [a nazirite] eats a grape seed, he is liable to two [sets of lashes] — for [violating the prohibition of] a grape seed, and for [violating] "from everything that is made [of the grapevine]" — and I thought: I will raise an objection against him, since the matter was not clear to him, and he would retract.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:1:2.hebrew: ולא ידענא דגמרא היא בידיה - מרביה, ומש"ה לא הדר ביה:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:1:2.english: And I did not know that it is a tradition in his hand - From his teacher, and for that reason he did not retract.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:2:1.hebrew: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה - אית ליה כרבי יוסי, מדקאמר "שני חרצנים וזג", משמע דלזג א' איכא ב' חרצנים:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:2:1.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya - holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, since he said, "Two ḥartzannim and a zag," which implies that for one zag there are two ḥartzannim.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:2:2.hebrew: פורצנין - דמשמע פנימי, כגון אפי' פרצידא דתותי קלא, דאמר בריש פ"ק דמס' תענית (ד' ד.) — דהיינו גרעינין:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:2:2.english: Purtzanin - Which implies [the] internal [part], such as: “Even a seed [partzida] beneath a clod [of earth],” which [the Gemara] states at the beginning of the first chapter of Tractate Ta’anit (4a) — that is, seeds.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:2:3.hebrew: עיצורין - משמע חיצונים, שסוחט מהמשקה, כדכתיב (בראשית מ׳:י״א): "ואשחט אותם", ומתרגמינן: "ועצרית יתהון":
Rashi on Nazir 39a:2:3.english: Itzurin - This implies the outer [parts], from which one squeezes out the juice, as it is written: “And I squeezed them” (Genesis 40:11), and we translate: “And I pressed them [va’atzarit yathon].”

Rashi on Nazir 39a:3:1.hebrew: גילח או שגילחוהו ליסטין - משמע: בין באונס בין ברצון, בתוך ימי נזירותו; בין בנזירות מרובה בין בנזירות מועטת:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:3:1.english: [If] he shaved or bandits shaved him - This implies: whether under duress or willingly, during the days of his naziriteship; whether in [the case of] a long naziriteship or in [the case of] a short naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:3:2.hebrew: סותר ל' יום - לפי שאין גידול שיער בפחות מל' יום:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:3:2.english: Negates thirty days - Because there is no [significant] hair growth in less than thirty days.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:3:3.english: Or if he pulled out any amount - That he plucked a bit at the tip of the hair.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:4:1.hebrew: איבעיא להו בינתא מלתחת רבי - האי שיער מלתחת רבי — בסמוך לבשר יוצא מן הראש וגדל, וראשו כדקאי קאי:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:4:1.english: A dilemma was raised before them: Does a hair grow from the bottom - [Does] this hair grow from the bottom — [meaning that] close to the flesh it emerges from the head and grows, while its tip remains as it is?

Rashi on Nazir 39a:4:2.hebrew: או מלעיל רבי - שראש השער מתגדל ויוצא מאיליו ומתגדל, ועיקרו כדקאי קאי:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:4:2.english: Or does it grow from above - That the tip of the hair grows and extends from itself and grows, while its root remains as it is.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:4:3.hebrew: למאי נפקא מינה לנזיר שגילחוהו ליסטים ושיירו בו כדי לכוף ראשו לעיקרו - א"א דהאי בינתא מלתחת רבי, הילכך למאי דאקדיש שקליה, וסותר נזירותו:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:4:3.english: What is the difference? Regarding a nazirite whom bandits shaved, and they left on him enough to bend its end to its root - If you say that this hair grows from the bottom, therefore, [the bandit] removed that which he had consecrated, and he negates his naziriteship.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:5:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת מלעיל רבי - הואיל ושיירו בו כדי לכוף בו ראשו לעיקרו, דאיכא למימר דמאי דאקדיש קאי — אכתי אית ליה למיעבד תגלחת מצוה, ואינו סותר:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:5:1.english: And if you say [that hair] grows from the top - Since they left on him enough [hair] to bend its tip to its root, so that it can be said that what he sanctified still remains, he can still perform the mitzvah shaving, and he does not negate [his days].

Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:1.hebrew: ת"ש מהאי אינבא חיה - לינטרי"ש בלע"ז, דהוא מביצי כינים:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:1.english: Come and hear from this live inba - Lentres in Old French, which is [one] of the eggs of lice.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:2.hebrew: דקיימא בעיקבא דבינתא - בעיקר השיער, סמוך לבשר:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:2.english: Which is situated at the root of the hair - At the root of the hair, close to the flesh.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:3.hebrew: ואי ס"ד - דהאי בינתא מלתחת רבי, אישתכח דכי נפיק שערא, נפיק אינבא לבר:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:3.english: And if it should enter your mind - That this hair grows from below, it turns out that as the hair emerges, the louse emerges outward.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:4.hebrew: ברישא דבינתא איבעי ליה למיקם - אינבא. אלא לאו ש"מ, מדקיימא אינבא בהדי בישרא, דמלעיל רבי, ואינבא בבינתא כדקאי קאי:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:4.english: It should have been situated on the end of the hair - [Namely,] the louse. Rather, is it not to be deduced from this, since the louse is situated next to the flesh, that [hair] grows from above, and the louse on the hair remains where it is?

Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:5.english: Actually, [hair] grows from the bottom - And as for that which [the louse] is not situated at the tip of the hair:

Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:6.hebrew: ואגב חיותא - דאית בה, נחתא ואזלה לתחת, לבהדי בישרא:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:6:6.english: And on account of [its] vitality - That it has, it continuously descends downward, next to the flesh:

Rashi on Nazir 39a:7:1.hebrew: ת"ש מדהאי אינבא מתה קיימא ברישא דבינתא - ואי ס"ד דהאי בינתא מלעיל רבי, אישתכח דכי היכי דמעיקרא קיימא בעיקרא דבינתא, הכי נמי איבעי לה למיקם השתא בעיקרא דבינתא:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:7:1.english: Come and hear from [the fact] that this dead louse is situated at the tip of the hair - And if it should enter your mind that this hair grows from above, it follows that just as it was originally situated at the root of the hair, so too it should now be situated at the root of the hair.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:7:2.hebrew: התם נמי משום דלית בה חילא - שאין בה כח, דהא הויא מתה:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:7:2.english: There too, because it has no strength - That it has no strength, since it is dead:

Rashi on Nazir 39a:7:3.hebrew: שרוגי קא משתרגא - משתמטא ואזלה כלפי רישא דבינתא, מש"ה קיימא לה התם, ולעולם מלעיל רבי:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:7:3.english: It slips along - It slips and moves toward the tip of the hair; that is why it is situated there, and in truth [hair] grows from above.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:8:1.hebrew: ת"ש מבלורית של כושיים דבתר דגדלין לה - שמקלעין את השיער זה בזה:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:8:1.english: Come and hear from the belorit of Cushites, that after they braid it - That they braid the hair into one another.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:8:2.hebrew: רפיא מלתחת - סמוך לבשר. ומדרפיא לתחת לבהדי בישרא ולא מלעיל, ש"מ דמלתחת הנץ השיער ויצא, מש"ה מרפו להני שערי מלתחת ולא מקלעי באידך בינתא. לעולם מלעיל רבי, והתם נמי איידי דקמטא — שמהדק בלורית ודוחק מעצמו למטה מחמת הגדל כששוכב עליה:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:8:2.english: It becomes loose underneath - Close to the flesh. And since it is loose below, next to the flesh, and not above, learn from this that the hair sprouted and emerged from below; for that reason, these hairs became loose below and are not braided with the other hair. [The Gemara answers:] Actually, [hair] grows from above; and there too, [it is loose] because it crumples — as [lying down] compresses the forelock, and it presses downward on its own on account of the braid when he lies upon it.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:8:3.hebrew: ומשיכבא הוא דרפיא - מחמת שכיבה הוא — ששוכב על הבלורית — רפיא לה מלתחת:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:8:3.english: And it is from lying [down] that it becomes loose - It is on account of lying [down] — in that he lies upon the belorit — [that] it becomes loose underneath.

Rashi on Nazir 39a:9:1.hebrew: מסקרתא דרפי עמרא מלתחת ותניא - כלומר, עד השתא בעינן לפרושי לך ממידי דסברא דלא תליא במידי דתניא, אלא השתא איכא למישמע מהא דסוקרין על העשירי לשום מעשר, דמתקשר כל השיער ביחד מחמת הצבע של סיקרא, ולבתר הכי רפיא עמרא מלתחת. ומאי טעמא? לאו משום דההוא דרפי רבי ליה לבתר הכי, וש"מ מלתחת רבי?! והא סברא הויא במידי דתניא:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:9:1.english: From the red dye, as the wool becomes loose underneath, and it was taught - That is to say, until now we sought to resolve [the matter] for you from a matter of reasoning that does not depend on anything taught [in a Tannaitic source]; but now, it can be deduced from this [practice] where they mark the tenth [animal] with red paint for the purpose of [animal] tithe, for all the wool binds together on account of the pigment of the red paint, and afterward the wool becomes loose underneath. And what is the reason? Is it not because that [wool] which is loose grew afterward, and conclude from this that [hair] grows from below?! And this reasoning is in [the context of] a matter that was taught [in a Tannaitic source].

Rashi on Nazir 39a:9:2.hebrew: ותו מדצבעי סביא דיקניהון - כי היכי דליתחזו דרדקיא, ובתר הכי חיורי דיקניהון — מתלבנים עיקרי שערי זקנם. ש"מ דמלתחת רבי, ומאי דקא קדיש האי נזיר — שקלוה מיניה, ואיבעי ליה למיסתר ולמימני נזירות אחרת, כי היכי דליקדוש שיער:
Rashi on Nazir 39a:9:2.english: And furthermore, from [the fact] that old men dye their beards - [They do so] so that they appear like young men; and after that, their beards turn white — the roots of their beard hair become white. Learn from this that [hair] grows from the bottom, and [therefore] that which this nazirite had sanctified, they [the bandits] took from him, and he must negate [his count] and count another naziriteship so that [his] hair will become sanctified.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:1:1.hebrew: והא אותביה חמש ומאחר דלא תניא מ"ט אותביה - כלומר: והלא רב פפא עצמו היה מקשה מיניה לאביי; ואי תנא לא תני ה' — מ"ט אותביה הוא:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:1:1.english: "And behold, he raised an objection to him [with] five, and since it is not taught, what is the reason that he raised an objection to him?" - That is to say: Was it not Rav Pappa himself who raised an objection from it against Abaye? And if the tanna did not teach five, what was the reason that he raised an objection to him?

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:1:2.hebrew: א"ר פפא אנא סברי לאו גמרא הוה בידיה - לכך בדיתי מלבי והוספתי על לשון הברייתא "חמש", ולהקשות לאביי — לראות אם מדעתו אמרה למימרא דידיה, דאז בקל יחזור מדבריו ולא ידחוק לתרץ הברייתא לדבריו. ולא ידענא דגמרא הוה בידיה; ואותבינן ולא הדר ביה, ולכך בחנתי דגמרא הוה בידיה:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:1:2.english: Rav Pappa said: "I reasoned that it was not a tradition in his hand" - Therefore, I devised [this] out of my own heart and added "five" to the wording of the baraita, in order to challenge Abaye — to see whether he stated his statement from his own reasoning, for then he would easily retract his statement and would not strain to reconcile the baraita to his words. But I did not know that it was a tradition in his hand; and I raised the objection to him and he did not retract, and thereby I tested [and confirmed] that it was a tradition in his hand.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:2:1.hebrew: מחרצנים מפורצנים - דהיינו הגרעינין. וכן במס' ע"ז (דף לד:): "פורצנים דיין נסך". ועצורין היינו הקליפה; "ואשחט" מתרגמי' "ועצרית", וסחיטה היינו בקליפה — שיסחוט הקליפה החיצונה שיש בה לחלוחית קצת, ולא בגרעיניה:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:2:1.english: “From ḥartzannim [is translated as] mi-purtzanin” - That is, the seeds. And so too in tractate Avodah Zarah (34b): “[Grape] seeds [purtzanin] of libation wine.” And itzurin is the skin; [for] “and I squeezed [va’eshḥat]” (Genesis 40:11) we translate [in the Targum as] “ve’atzarit,” and squeezing applies to the skin — that one squeezes the outer skin, which has some moisture in it, and not its seeds.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:3:1.hebrew: סתם נזירות ל' יום - כבר שנינו זה בפ"ק (דף ה.). ואיידי דבעי למתני "גילח או שגלחוהו לסטים סותר ל' יום", תני נמי "סתם [נזירות] שלשים יום". וטעמא דסותר ל' יום — משום דבעיא נזירות שיעלה לו תגלחת של מצוה, כדי שיהא שערו גדל כפי שראוי לגדל כסתם נזירות, דהיינו שלשים יום. ומיירי שגלחוהו ביום מלאת, שהרי אם גלחוהו (בשנים) או יותר, למה יסתור את הכל? איך יחזור וימנה מה שמנה כבר?! ואולי הכי נמי קאמר: סותר עד שיהו שערותיו כדי שלשים יום; כך נמצא בפירוש ה"ר יצחק. והלכך, בנזירות של [ס'], אם גלחוהו ביום שלשים אינו סותר כלום, דאיכא עדיין גידול שער קודם יום תגלחת; ואם גלחוהו אחר שכלו ימיו [ואין] גידול שער, סותר [ל'] לרבנן, כדמוכח בגמרא:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:3:1.english: "An unspecified naziriteship is thirty days" - We already learned this in the first chapter (5a). And since [the Tanna] needed to teach, "If he shaved or bandits shaved him, he negates thirty days," he also taught, "An unspecified [naziriteship] is thirty days." And the reason that he negates thirty days is that naziriteship requires that the mitzvah shaving count for him [only] when his hair has grown as is fitting to grow in an unspecified naziriteship, which is thirty days. And [the Mishnah] is dealing with [a case] where they shaved him on the day of completion; for if they shaved him (on two [days]) or more, why should he negate everything? How could he go back and count what he already counted?! And perhaps [the Mishnah] also means this: he negates [the completion and must wait] until his hair is [grown] equivalent to thirty days; so it is found in the commentary of Rabbeinu Yitzchak. And therefore, in a naziriteship of [sixty], if they shaved him on the thirtieth day, he does not negate anything, as there is still hair growth before the day of shaving; and if they shaved him after his days were completed [and there is no] hair growth, he negates [thirty] according to the Rabbis, as is proven in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:3:2.hebrew: נזיר שגילח בין במספרים או שסיפסף - פירוש: תלש. ״כל שהוא״ — אפי' שער אחד, לוקה עליו. מיירי שעוקר השיער מעיקרו, ומשחית מן השורש כעין תער, דלוקה מקרא ד״תער לא יעבור על ראשו״, דמרבינן בגמרא שאר המעבירין:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:3:2.english: "A nazirite who shaved, whether with scissors, or if he pulled out [sifsef]" - Explanation: [Sifsef means] he plucked [hair]. [And as for] "any amount" — he receives lashes even for a single hair. [This] is dealing with [a case where] he uproots the hair from its base and destroys [it] from the root in the manner of a razor, for he receives lashes by virtue of the verse "A razor shall not pass over his head" (Numbers 6:5), as we include other means of hair removal in the Gemara.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:4:1.hebrew: שער מלתחת רבי - משרשו, מעיקרו, הוא מגביה וגדל: מה שהשער גדל מתמר ועולה, הסמוך לראש אחר ימים יהיה ברחוק; או מלעיל רבי — מראש השער הולך וגדל, אבל סמוך לראש אין [זז] ממקומו:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:4:1.english: [Does] hair grow from below - [Meaning,] from its root, from its base, it rises and grows: as the hair grows, it shoots upward and rises, [so that what is] adjacent to the head will after [some] days be at a distance [from the head]; or [does it] grow from above — from the tip of the hair it continuously grows, but [the part] adjacent to the head does not move from its place.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:4:2.hebrew: ושיירו בו כדי לכוף ראשו לעיקרו - בכל שער ושער. [שיעורא] בעלמא הוא, ובסמוך אמר שבו ליגדל השער בז' ימים, ובכך יש חשיבות שער:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:4:2.english: "And they left on him enough to bend its end to its root" - [This means] on each and every hair. It is merely a [standard] measure, and nearby [the Gemara] says that it takes seven days for the hair to grow [this amount], and with that [growth] the hair has significance.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:5:1.hebrew: ואי אמרת מלתחת רבי נזירותו הא שקליה - כלומר: השיער שהקדיש ביום נזרו — זה נטלו וגלחו, וזה ששיירו בו כדי לכוף, אין זה משער שהיה לו משעת קבלת נזרו, אלא צמח בו אחר כן; וסותר, אחרי שלא נשתייר מאותו שער שהיה בקבלת נזרו. ואי אמרת מלעיל רבי — מאי דאקדיש קאי, דאותו ששיירו ודאי מאותו שיער שהקדיש, ובכך הוי שיעור חשוב, ואינו סותר כלום:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:5:1.english: And if you say that it grows from the bottom, he has removed the hair of the naziriteship - That is to say: the hair that he consecrated on the day of his nazirite vow — this he took and shaved off; and that which was left of it [amounting to] enough to bend [the tip to its root] is not from the hair that he had from the time of the acceptance of his nazirite vow, but rather grew on him afterward; and [therefore] he negates [his count of days], since nothing remained of that hair which was [present] at the acceptance of his nazirite vow. But if you say that it grows from the top, that which he consecrated still exists, for that which was left is certainly of that hair which he consecrated, and thereby it is a significant measure, and he does not negate anything.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:6:1.hebrew: ת"ש מהאי אינבא - פירוש: ביצי כינים. "דקאי בעיקרא" — פירוש: בעיקר השיער, סמוך לראש, ולא תצא משם בגידול שער. ש"מ דמלעיל רבי, ומש"ה השער שסמוך לראש כדקאי קאי; דאי מלתחת רבי, ברישא דבינתא בעי למיקם האינבא, והשער הולך וגדל מעיקרו ולמעלה:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:6:1.english: "Come and hear from this inba" - Explanation: Lice eggs [nits]. "Which stands at the base" — explanation: At the base of the hair, adjacent to the head, and it does not move from there as the hair grows. Conclude from this that [hair] grows from above, and for that reason the hair that is adjacent to the head remains standing as it is; for if it grew from below, the inba should have been situated at the tip of the hair, with the hair continuously growing from its root upward.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:6:2.hebrew: אגב חיותא נחת ואזיל - אינבא, הוא יורד למטה כשהשער גדל מלמעלה מרום הראש:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:6:2.english: "Because it is alive, it continuously descends" - The louse: it descends downward as the hair grows upward above the crown of the head.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:7:1.hebrew: ברישא דבינתא - לאו ברישא, אלא ברחוק מן הראש קאמר:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:7:1.english: "At the end of the hair" - [The Gemara] does not mean [literally] at the end, but rather it means at a distance from the head.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:7:2.hebrew: ואי ס"ד מלעיל רבי בעיקרא דבינתא בעי למיקם - [במקום] שעמדה כשהיתה חיה, שהרי שם מתה:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:7:2.english: "And if it should enter your mind that [hair] grows from on top, it should be situated at the root of the hair" - [In the place] where it stood when it was alive, for it died there.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:7:3.hebrew: התם נמי משום דלית בה חילא - כלומר: בזו, שהרי מתה — שמטה ואזלה, מחוברת ויורדת לראש השער שהוא תלוי למטה לצד הארץ, ואין לה כח להאחז למעלה לצד הראש:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:7:3.english: "There too, because it has no strength" - That is to say: in [the case of] this [louse], since it is dead, it slips and goes [down], [remaining] attached and descending to the tip of the hair, which hangs downward toward the ground, and it has no strength to hold on above, toward the head.

Tosafot on Nazir 39a:8:1.hebrew: ת"ש מבלורית של כושיים - שמניחים בלוריות [בראשיהם] לשם ע"ז, ובשער אין מגלחין כל סביב ראשו, ומה שהיו מניחין — הן גידלו אותה כקליעה סמוך לראש, ואינו מהודק כבראשונה. ואי מלעיל רבי — אמאי? אלא ודאי מלתחת רבי, ונדחית הקליעה לפנים והלאה מן הראש, ונמצא כי בשער שסמוך לראש אינו קלוע, ולכך הוי כפרוש. ומשני: "איידי דקמטא היא משיכבא רפיא" — ממה שהוא שוכב עליה נוסעת ממקומה ונרפית סמוך לראש:
Tosafot on Nazir 39a:8:1.english: "Come and hear from the belorit of gentiles [Cushites]" - For they leave locks of hair [on their heads] for idolatrous purposes, and regarding the hair, they do not shave all around his head; and that which they would leave, they braided like a plait close to the head, and [over time] it is not tight as at first. And if [hair] grows from above [at the tips], why [would it become loose]? Rather, it certainly grows from below [at the roots], and the braid is pushed forward and away from the head, and it turns out that the hair adjacent to the head is not braided, and therefore it is as if spread out. And [the Gemara] answers: "Since it crumples from lying down, it becomes loose" — from the fact that he lies upon it, it shifts from its place and becomes loosened close to the head.
